issues.description: Test changed to pass a zero-amount/zero-puzzle-hash addition just to satisfy validation — that's not a test fix, that's hiding a regression in the public API
issues.detail: The old `cat_spend` accepted `additions=[]` and fell back to `amount`/`inner_address`. The new code passes `request.additions` through directly when not None, so an empty list now fails `CreateSignedTransaction.__post_init__` (`len(self.additions) < 1`). Rather than preserving the prior behavior, the test was edited to feed a junk Addition. Existing callers in the wild will break. Either keep `additions=[]` semantically equivalent to None, or document the breakage.

issues.description: `send_transaction` silently dropped its prefix check in favor of `ensure_valid_address` — behavior change masquerading as refactor
issues.detail: The old code rejected with `"Unexpected Address Prefix"`. The new code calls `ensure_valid_address` with `allowed_types={AddressType.XCH}`, which raises a different error message and accepts/rejects different inputs depending on `AddressType.XCH`'s definition. A refactor that changes user-visible error contracts isn't a refactor. Either preserve the message or call it out in the commit.

issues.description: Three-patches problem — this commit does refactor + new fields + behavior changes + test edits in one diff
issues.detail: Extracting `cat_discrepancy_validation` is one patch. Adding `extra_delta`/`tail_reveal`/`tail_solution`/`puzzle_decorator` to `CreateSignedTransaction` is another. Forwarding `send_transaction` and `cat_spend` is a third. Plumbing `puzzle_decorator_override`/`cat_discrepancy` in `_generate_signed_transaction` is a fourth. Bisecting a regression here means reading the whole diff. Split it.

issues.description: `puzzle_decorator` field comment admits it's a hack — bake in the limitation properly or don't ship it
issues.detail: The comment says "as a slight hack, we'll specify that only Clawback is supported." Either the type system enforces the constraint cleanly (a discriminated union, a single field, whatever) or you ship the general type with runtime validation. Shipping a `list[ClawbackPuzzleDecoratorOverride] | None` named generically `puzzle_decorator` with an apology comment is the worst of both options. Future maintainer will curse you.

issues.description: Duplicated `# type: ignore[arg-type]` block in `cat_discrepancy_validation` — the comment says mypy is wrong, fix it
issues.detail: The function admits "Curious that mypy doesn't see the elif and know that none of these are None." The fix is two lines: assert the three are not None after the elif, or do explicit None checks. Don't ship three `type: ignore` comments and a confused comment to a shared helper. This was tolerable buried in a property; it's not tolerable as a public helper.

issues.description: Discarding the return value of `get_wallet` with a "# opportunity to raise" comment is sloppy
issues.detail: If the call exists only for its side effect of raising, write `# Validate wallet exists and is the right type` and be explicit. "Opportunity to raise" reads like the author wasn't sure why it was kept. Also: `create_signed_transaction` will look up the wallet again, so this is a double lookup. Either fold the check into the callee or drop it.

review.summary: NEEDS-WORK. The intent — collapse `send_transaction` and `cat_spend` onto `create_signed_transaction` — is right and overdue. The execution does too many things in one diff and quietly breaks the existing contract. The test was patched to feed a junk `Addition` instead of preserving the empty-additions fallback, which is a tell that real callers will break. `ensure_valid_address` replaces a specific prefix error with a different one. The `puzzle_decorator` field ships with an apology comment in place of design. Split the patch, preserve the public API, and remove the `type: ignore` triplet from the shared helper. Then it lands.
